'''Shibagahara Kofun''' (芝ヶ原古墳), also known as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun, is a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} located in Terada Ōtani, {{ill|Jōyō, Kyoto|en|Jōyō, Kyoto|qid=Q817276|lt=Jōyō, Kyoto}}, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan. Part of the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群}} (specifically the Shibagahara subgroup), the kofun has been designated a National Historic Site, and its burial goods are designated as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}}.

== Overview ==
Shibagahara Kofun was built atop a hill in the northern part of Jōyō City in southern Kyoto Prefecture{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群}}, which includes prominent tombs such as the {{ill|Kutsukawa Kurumazuka Kofun|ja|久津川車塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kutsukawa Kurazuka Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11369464}}, and is specifically part of the Shibagahara subgroup (referred to as Shibagahara No. 12 Kofun){{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. Excavations were carried out in 1986 (Shōwa 61) prior to residential development{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}, and the site has since been preserved as a historic park.

While originally a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}}, the front section of the mound has been flattened, leaving a remaining length of 21 meters{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The mound lacks stepped construction and exterior stone covering ({{ill|fukiishi|fr|Fukiishi|ja|葺石|zh|葺石|qid=Q11621213}}){{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}} and is surrounded by a moat{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. The burial facility consists of a composite wooden coffin measuring 3 meters in length and 0.8 meters in width{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. The burial pit measures 4.7 meters in length and 2.5 meters in width{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}. Numerous grave goods, including bronze mirrors, bracelets, and beads, were recovered, with the discovery of bronze bracelets being particularly rare examples<ref name="Joyo City Tourism Association"/>.

The kofun is dated to the mid-3rd century (or the early 3rd century according to some sources) during the early {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}}<ref name="Joyo City Tourism Association">[http://xn--6oqz6c35b6zh48ipn2e0ys.jp/html/kankou/rekisi3.html#32 National Historic Sites and {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} > Shibagahara Kofun] (Joyo City Tourism Association).</ref>. It is considered one of the most prominent kofun of its time in the southern Yamashiro region, predating the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|qid=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Otsukayama Kofun}}{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}.

The site was designated a National Historic Site in 1989 (Heisei 1)<ref name="historic-site"/> and its grave goods were designated National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} in 1990 (Heisei 2)<ref name="cultural-property"/>. In 2016, the broader {{ill|Kutsukawa Kofun Cluster|ja|久津川古墳群}}, encompassing four additional kofun, was also designated a National Historic Site<ref name="Agency of Cultural Affairs">{{PDFlink|[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/pdf/2016061701_besshi03.pdf "Regarding the designation of Historic Sites"]}} (Agency of Cultural Affairs press release, June 17, 2016).</ref><ref>Ministry of Education, Science and Culture Notice No. 144, October 3, 2016.</ref>; however, Shibagahara Kofun itself is not included in this extended designation.

== Excavation History ==
* '''1986 (Showa 61):''' Excavation conducted from June to August by Joyo City Board of Education<ref name="historic-site"/>.
* '''1989 (Heisei 1):''' Designated as a National Historic Site on September 6<ref name="historic-site"/>.
* '''1990 (Heisei 2):''' Grave goods designated as National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} on June 29<ref name="cultural-property"/>.
* '''2012 (Heisei 24):''' Expanded designation of historic site boundaries<ref name="historic-site"/>.

== Mound Details ==
[[File:Shibagahara Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Rear section of the mound}}]]
The mound's dimensions are as follows{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}:
* '''Rear section'''
** North-South: 21 meters
** East-West: 19 meters
* '''Front section'''
** Length: Approximately 3.5 meters
* '''Constricted section'''
** Width: 11.6 meters

== burial goods ==
[[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 四獣鏡.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Four-animal bronze mirror}}{{small|Exhibited at Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan).}}]]
[[File:芝ヶ原古墳出土 銅釧.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Bronze bracelet}}]]
Key burial goods recovered from the coffin include the following{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}:
* '''Four-animal bronze mirror''' (仿製鏡) – 1 piece (12 cm diameter, Chinese imitation mirror)
* '''Bronze bracelets''' (同笵) – 2 pieces (matching set)
* '''Jadeite magatama beads''' – 8 pieces
* '''Jasper tubular beads''' – 187 pieces
* '''Glass small beads''' – 1,276 pieces
* '''Yariganna chisel''' (iron adze) – 1 piece
Additionally, fragments of {{ill|Shōnai-style pottery|ja|庄内式土器}}, including double-rimmed jars and high-footed bowls, were found in the gravel layer above the burial pit{{Sfn|Kyoto Prefecture Archaeological Intypeation No. 104|2007|11=36-37}}{{Sfn|Shibagahara Kofun (National Historic Site)}}. These items are preserved at the Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan)<ref name="Joyo City Tourism Association"/>.

== Historic Site ==
=== Important Cultural Property (National Designation) ===
* '''Burial goods excavated from Shibagahara Kofun, Kyoto Prefecture''' – Designated June 29, 1990<ref name="cultural-property">{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|10078|burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun}}</ref>.

=== National Historic Site ===
* '''Shibagahara Kofun''' – Designated September 6, 1989, with expanded boundaries on January 24, 2012<ref name="historic-site">{{国指定文化財等データベース|401|1750|Shibagahara Kofun}}</ref>.

== Related Facilities ==
* '''Joyo City Historical Folk Museum (Gorigorikan)''' (Terada Imahoricho, Joyo City) – Houses and exhibits burial goods from Shibagahara Kofun.
